about: Living Roots Wine & Co. was founded in 2016 by Sebastian and Colleen Hardy. Seb comes from six generations of South Australian winemakers; Colleen, a Rochester-area native, met him while working a vintage at the Hardy family’s Tintara winery. They make wine in both of their home regions: Finger Lakes whites and sparkling wines, first at Rochester’s only urban winery on University Avenue and now also at a winery on the family’s Shale Creek Vineyard above Keuka Lake, and reds in the Adelaide Hills.

Vidal Blanc is a French-American hybrid grape, hardy enough for cold winters and slow to ripen, with thick skins that let it hang on the vine long into autumn. That makes it a classic for late-harvest and ice wines in New York and Canada. For this wine Living Roots leaves the grapes out into early winter, picking after the first snows, when they have shrivelled and concentrated. The fermentation is then stopped early, leaving a naturally semi-sweet wine with high acidity to match.

The winemakers describe juicy peach and melon running into tropical fruit, with pretty floral notes and a touch of beeswax, all lifted by bright acidity. Vidal also turns up in the winery’s Session Gold, an experimental skin-macerated blend of Cayuga White and Vidal on the skins of aromatic grapes, which VinePair counted among the best orange wines of 2025.
